Power-Systems Engineer said about it: I read the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60) which accepts 8-40 V input and delivers regulated 12 V at up to 3 A with 85 percent efficiency, which covers the swing from the low-wind volts (E37) 6.50 V to the top volts (E36) 14.3 V; after the bridge the net power (E38) 26.0 W gives regulated load power (E66) 22.1 W, about a laptop charger, so droop is plus-minus 1 percent not loss of feed.
Power-Systems Engineer said about it: I read the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60) which needs 8 V minimum input, while low-wind volts (E37) are 6.50 V below that though top volts (E36) 14.3 V fit; I recompute because 220 Kv cannot span the window, and 170-180 Kv gives 8.41 V low and 18.5 V top (E76) inside 8-40 V, about a laptop charger holding steady instead of dropping out.
Safety-Control Integrator said about it: I take from the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60) that it needs 8 V minimum, so the old 6.50 V low-wind volts in the open-circuit volts at low wind (E37) would starve regulation while the revised 8.41 V low and 18.5 V top in the required Kv revision (E76) stays inside 8 to 40 V; with 18.5 V the revised dump power (E78) is 85.6 W, about one household bulb for seconds, so the 0.673 s crossing in the upgraded stop (E70) is conservative and the 0.800 N-m hold still does the parking.
Aero-Rotor Lead said about it: The speeds 1.43e+03 RPM, meaning shaft turns per minute, in the rpm at 5 m/s (E14) to 3.15e+03 RPM in the rpm at 11 m/s (E13) are unchanged, while the old 6.50 V in the open-circuit volts at low wind (E37) sits below the 8 V minimum I take from the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60) which needs 8 V minimum, and the revised 8.41 V low and 18.5 V top in the required Kv revision (E76) sit inside 8 to 40 V, so I support the blocking objection to the locomotive-grid feed (O2).
Structures-Survival Engineer said about it: I read the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60) which accepts 8-40 V input and delivers regulated 12 V, which from structures side means the revised 8.41 V low and 18.5 V top (E76) only move volts inside the body with no added thrust; survival thrust (E22) 37.3 N with moment (E23) 13.1 N·m still give deflection (E26) 0.516 mm and stress (E27) 16.6 Megapascal (MPa), meaning million newtons per square metre, about 17 times below typical 276 MPa yield in the Aluminum 6061-T6 — Material Datasheet (E55), like a heavy shopping bag on a scaffold pole.
Manager said about it: The old low volts 6.50 V in the open-circuit volts at low wind (E37) sat below the 8 V minimum in the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A (E60), while the revised 8.41 V low and 18.5 V top in the required Kv revision (E76) sit inside 8 to 40 V, so the blocking objection to the locomotive-grid feed (O2) is resolved and the dump rises from the old 51.1 W in the dump resistor power (E39) to 85.6 W in the revised dump power (E78), which supersedes it.
Safety-Control Integrator said about it: Safety-Control Integrator: For Power-Systems Engineer and Manager, I take up the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60) which accepts 8 to 40 V input and delivers regulated 12 V, which from shutdown side means the load-present tap stays alive across wind and will not false-trip at light wind.
Aero-Rotor Lead said about it: Speeds stay 1.43e+03 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM), meaning shaft turns per minute, in the rpm at 5 m/s (E14) to 3.15e+03 RPM in the rpm at 11 m/s (E13) with shaft 3.27 W in the shaft power at 5 m/s (E11), while revised volts 8.41 V low to 18.5 V top in the required Kv revision (E76) sit inside the window I take up from the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60) which needs 8 V minimum to make regulated 12 V, where Kv, meaning turns per volt, is 170 to 180.
Structures-Survival Engineer said about it: For the Manager, I take up the Buck-Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A (E60) which accepts 8 to 40 V input and delivers regulated 12 V, which from structures side means the revised volts (E76) 8.41 V low to 18.5 V top only move volts inside the body with no added thrust or heat into the post.
Power-Systems Engineer said about it: Low regulated power is 2.08 W in the low-wind regulated power (E80) from 3.27 W shaft in the shaft power at 5 m/s (E11), while high regulated stays 22.1 W in the regulated load power (E66), with volts 8.41 V to 18.5 V in the required Kv revision (E76) inside 8 to 40 V in the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60), where Kv means speed per volt; like a night-light at light wind rising to laptop level at strong wind, which is ordinary.
Manager said about it: Shaft 3.27 W in the shaft power at 5 m/s (E11) to regulated 22.1 W in the regulated load power (E66) at speeds 1.43e+03 to 3.15e+03 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM), meaning shaft turns per minute, in the rpm at 5 m/s (E14) and the rpm at 11 m/s (E13), with volts 8.41 to 18.5 V in the required Kv revision (E76) inside 8 to 40 V in the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60), where Kv means turns per volt; low regulated 2.08 W in the low-wind regulated power (E80) confirms light-wind feed.
